response: Dementia and aphasia in motor neuron disease (MND) is indeed an underrecognized association. Research has shown that the prevalence of cognitive impairment in MND is higher than previously reported. Language deficits, particularly anomia (difficulty naming objects), may be relatively frequent in MND patients. However, aphasia (a condition that affects an individual's ability to communicate effectively) in MND may be masked by dysarthria (speech difficulties) and can be missed if not specifically examined. Therefore, it is essential to thoroughly assess MND patients for cognitive and language impairments to provide accurate diagnoses and appropriate care.
